label: Research only. Not a recommendation to buy or sell. This desk never places trades. Stocks only, no option contracts.

keeper._note: Update keeper (features.self_heal_keeper). One keeper job sleeps until check_after_min minutes past each New York slot (weekdays, NYSE holidays skipped) and starts that slot's update only if it did not run and the last update started over min_gap_min minutes ago. After chunk_min minutes (at most 340; GitHub stops a job at 360) it starts the next keeper. Turn the switch off and the keeper stops at its next wake and does not chain. At verify_after_min past each slot it checks that the slot's run succeeded and that data/meta.json price_as_of reached that day. A failed slot gets one retry (max_tries 2 means the run plus one retry, never more); a run still going is looked at again every recheck_min minutes. Stale data after a success is recorded in the keeper run, not retried. It only triggers the normal slots and at most one retry of a failed slot, so Yahoo traffic does not grow.

light_mode._note: Light mode. features.light_mode shows or hides the Theme switch (Dark, Light, Match device) at the top of the left menu. With the switch hidden the whole desk stays dark. default_theme is what a phone or iPad sees before it picks one: dark, light, or device. The pick is saved on that device. match_device_option shows the Match device button. Colors only; nothing new is downloaded.

vcp._note: VCP scanner (vcp.html). A stock is listed only when the trend template is 8 of 8 and it has at least min_pullbacks tightening pullbacks (default 2, the green VCP tag). READY is that tag at or under the buy line. BROKEN OUT today is a close over it on at least 1.5 times the 50-day volume. WATCHING is 8 of 8 with two or more pullbacks and the close already over the buy line without that volume, or an open trade whose buy printed at 8 of 8. A name with only one pullback stays off the list. Set min_pullbacks to 1 to list those as WATCHING again. show_weaker_trend brings back stocks under 8 of 8, labeled WATCHING (trend not 8/8) and listed last, and does not use min_pullbacks. Those rows never feed Buy setups or Leaders. Nothing new is downloaded.

scanner_groups._note: Technical and Fundamental split (features.split_tech_fund). With it on, the left menu puts every screener page under a Technical or a Fundamental heading, in the order listed here, and the Chart Viewer gets a Technical | Fundamental switch (chart_viewer.group_toggle) whose list picker, All technical stocks or All fundamental stocks list, and Why box show only that side. Each key is a page id (the name in chart-viewer.html?list=...): vcp, box, flag, qullamaggie, marios, ep (Episodic pivot), gapup (Gap Up), week52 (52-week), breakouts (52-week breakouts), volume (High volume), pullbacks, breakdowns, trends, wheel, canslim, leaders, growth, quality, dividend, scorecard (Stock scorecard), and top (Top stocks). The value is technical or fundamental; any other word leaves that page where it was and out of both. Buy setups and Watchlist are in both sides of the Chart Viewer. Today, Watchlist, Buy setups, Trading Floor, Paper Test, Alerts, Backtest, Options, Earnings, Sentiment, Financials, Macro, and the market pages (Gainers and losers, Breadth, Sector performance, Heatmaps, under Market) are not screeners and stay outside both. Turn features.split_tech_fund off for exactly the old menu and viewer. Nothing new is downloaded.

chart_viewer._note: Chart Viewer page (chart-viewer.html). Full-screen charts you swipe through, one stock at a time. It reads the saved daily bars and the scanner files only. No new downloads. include_trends is on, so the Trends list is in the picker on the Technical side: only Uptrend rows from the saved trends.csv, which means the price is above the 20, 50, 100, and 200-day averages. The Why box uses that label and the SMA alignment. Those stocks count in All technical stocks and in All scanner stocks. Turn include_trends off to leave the list and those counts out. features.trends still turns the Trends page itself off. Every option has its own on/off switch. chart_touch_pan is on, so a one-finger drag moves the chart back and forward through the saved history (about five years) and a pinch zooms; only a quick flick (swipe_max_ms or less, at least swipe_min_px wide) changes the chart, and a sideways swipe on the header row (ticker, price, counter) always does. The chip bar changes the chart only when every chip fits; on a phone, where it is wider than the screen, a swipe there scrolls the chips instead. drag_mode_toggle shows the Drag chip that switches between Drag: move chart and Drag: next chart on each device. range_months and range_months_phone set only the first view, which fills the width once the chart is laid out and is put back after full screen or a turn of the screen; a range you dragged to is kept when the screen turns or full screen opens or closes, until a range chip is tapped; range_chips shows 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All. fit_wide_ranges is on, so All, or any range too long to fit, fills the space left of the Why box with as much history as fits at the thinnest bar spacing (min_bar_spacing, 0.3 px) and keeps the newest candle just left of the box, like the India desk; turn it off to go back to the old view, which on an iPhone showed only a couple of bars for All. native_fullscreen_ios is off, so on an iPhone or iPad Full screen fills the page without Safari's own full screen and its grey X over the stock name; turn it on to use Safari's full screen again. Computers always use the browser's full screen. group_toggle shows the Technical | Fundamental switch at the top when features.split_tech_fund is on: the list picker, All technical stocks or All fundamental stocks, and the Why box show only that side (Buy setups and Watchlist show in both), and the last pick is saved on each device; default_group (technical or fundamental) is where a device starts. The sides come from the scanner_groups block. With group_toggle or features.split_tech_fund off the viewer is the old single one with All scanner stocks. why_box_top_left is on, so the Why box sits at the top left of the chart and the newest candle stays a small fixed gap left of the price axis on every chart; turn it off to put the box back in the lower right and leave room for it again. weekly_toggle shows Daily | Weekly. Daily is the start. Weekly bars are built in the browser from the saved daily bars (Monday to Friday: first open, highest high, lowest low, last close, volume added up, and a week that is not finished still counts). Averages are worked out on the bars on screen, so MA 10 on Weekly is 10 weeks. range_months_weekly (24) and range_months_weekly_phone (12) are the first view for Weekly, 2 years or 1 year. hide_range_chips is on, so the 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All buttons are hidden; turn it off to bring them back (range_chips can still hide them). bars_toggle shows Candles | Bars. Candles is the start. Bars are a high-to-low line with a left tick for the open and a right tick for the close. Up bars are blue (bar_up, and bar_up_light in light mode) and down bars are pink (bar_down, and bar_down_light). Each pick is saved on the device. dense_default is on, so every chart opens at the same candle width (target_bar_spacing 5.8 px, the iPad portrait daily chart): a phone, an iPad, daily, and weekly all use it, and the newest candle stays 12 px left of the price axis. min_bar_spacing_px (3) is the thinnest those candles get, and max_bar_spacing_px (8) stops a short history from stretching fat. Turn dense_default off to open on range_months / range_months_phone and the weekly month spans again. Turn the whole page off with features.chart_viewer.

chart_colors._note: Moving average line colors, shared by every price chart: the Chart Viewer (chart-viewer.html) and the expand-in-place row charts on the scanner and list pages. The same color is used for the line, its toggle chip, and its value in the legend. ma_colors is for dark mode: MA 10 green, MA 20 orange, MA 50 blue, MA 150 yellow, MA 200 red. The row charts' SMA 50, SMA 150, and SMA 200 use the 50, 150, and 200 colors; their SMA 21 and EMA lines keep their own colors. ma_colors_light is used in light mode, with slightly darker shades so each line still shows on white (yellow is #ca8a04). Each value is a #RRGGBB color. A missing or bad value falls back to these defaults. Colors only; nothing new is downloaded.

episodic_pivot._note: Episodic Pivot scan. Original Qullamaggie and Stockbee rules on cached daily bars, earnings dates, and Yahoo profiles. No new downloads. Every rule has an on/off switch and its number here. Percents are whole numbers (10 means 10%). Money is US dollars. The nick_ switches are Nick's own extra filters and are off by default. The time stop only flags NO FOLLOW-THROUGH; it never closes a trade. Turn the whole page off with features.scanner_ep.

gap_up._note: Gap Up scanner (gap-up.html). A true gap: the open is above the previous day's high (true_gap_only off measures from the previous close instead). Gap % is open divided by the previous high, minus 1; the gap over the previous close is shown too. min_gap_filter on keeps only gaps of at least min_gap_pct, a whole percent (3.0 means 3%); off, any size of true gap counts. Gap-day volume must be at least vol_mult times the average of the vol_avg_days sessions before the gap day. The last close must be at least min_price dollars, and the average daily traded value (close times volume) over the last liquidity_days sessions at least min_dollar_volume, the same $3 million 50-day floor the Episodic Pivot scan uses. Hold rule: no close since the gap day below the gap day's low; a close equal to the low still holds. Gap days come from the last lookback_days trading days, today included, and the newest holding gap is the row. skip_stale leaves out a stock whose last bar is older than SPY's. Gap Up does not feed Buy setups. Every rule has an on/off switch. Cached daily bars only. No new downloads. Turn the whole page off with features.scanner_gap_up.

qullamaggie._note: Qullamaggie breakout scan on cached daily bars. Every rule has an on/off switch and its numbers here. Percents are whole numbers (3.5 means 3.5%). Prices and money are in US dollars. Marios uses these for the shared rules unless the marios block sets its own.

marios._note: Marios breakout scan. Shared entry rules come from the qullamaggie block. Keys here are Marios's own and win over the qullamaggie block.

trading_floor_paper._note: Paper test of the Trading Floor's BUY calls with FAKE MONEY (paper-test.html, features.trading_floor_paper). It starts with start_cash fake dollars on the first full run (Nov 3, 2026) and only goes forward; nothing is replayed. Each BUY call on a full run waits for the next session and is bought at that session's open, on the next full run, from the saved daily bar. A call is skipped when the stock is already held or waiting (skip_if_held), when max_open positions are open or waiting, or when free fake cash is under one position. Each position is position_pct percent of start_cash, in fractional shares rounded to share_decimals (fractional_shares off buys whole shares). With skip_gap_past_plan on, a stock that opens at or under its stop or at or over target 1 is not bought. Stop and target 1 are frozen at the call. Every daily bar from the entry day on: an open at or under the stop sells at the open; an open at or over the target sells at the open; a day that touches both counts as the stop; else the stop or target price; after time_stop_days trading days (the entry day is day 1) it sells at the close. The state is in data/paper_trades.csv, data/paper_equity.csv, and data/paper_summary.csv. Only the full run changes them, and running the same day twice changes nothing. No real orders, no broker, no alerts, no new downloads. Rules: docs/trading_floor_paper_rules.md.

trading_floor._note: Trading Floor page (trading-floor.html, features.trading_floor). Six desk roles debate today's top picks: the Buy setups list in its own order, then (fill_from_scanners) stocks READY or BROKEN OUT today on at least fill_min_scanners pattern scanners, max_stocks in all. News, Scout, Charts, Skeptic, and Sentiment each give +1, 0, or -1 and the Chief adds them: Charts veto (no valid entry, stop, and target) is SKIP; a total of verdict.buy_min_total or more with no Skeptic hard no is BUY; verdict.wait_min_total or more is WAIT; under that is SKIP. News uses the desk's stored headlines first; only picks with none get one free Google News RSS request each, on the full run, once a day (news.google_news), cached in cache/trading_floor_news.csv. Percents are whole numbers (5.0 means 5%). Volume ratios compare today with the 50 sessions before it, like the High volume page. Every check has its own on/off switch. Research only: no orders, no broker, no alerts. Rules in plain words: docs/trading_floor_rules.md.

liquid_names._note: Other common stocks (features.liquid_names and indexes.liquid). On the full run the desk reads the Nasdaq stock screener, keeps names with a market cap of at least min_market_cap dollars that the Nasdaq Trader symbol files call a common stock, and adds the ones that are not already on an index until the scored list reaches max_stocks. No Yahoo request. Off leaves the S&P lists, the Nasdaq-100, and the growth names as they are.

slow_sources._note: Yahoo profiles and Nasdaq 13F/insider on a full run. Each name is its own request, so the whole daily list no longer fits in the job. One run refreshes at most batch_per_run names: any still missing, then the ones last refreshed longest ago. A name already refreshed inside refresh_every_days waits. Hourly runs still reuse the cache and make no extra calls.

sec_facts._note: A full run fills company facts for the whole universe (full_universe). It prefers the official nightly companyfacts.zip (use_bulk_zip) and falls back to one request per company at under 8/sec. The older daily slice (batch_per_run, refresh_every_days, features.sec_rolling) is used only when full_universe is off. cik_overrides replaces a ticker that the SEC ticker file points at the wrong filer. XOM is Exxon Mobil Corporation, CIK 0000034088. HONA, SPCX, and VYLR already point at the companies that own those tickers; they have no 10-K yet, so yearly rows stay blank.

earnings_calendar._note: Nasdaq earnings calendar on a full run. One request per weekday for the next days_ahead calendar days, starting from today so the window crosses into January by itself when the year changes. A failed fetch keeps the saved calendar. Next earnings is filled only where it is still missing.

incremental_prices._note: Daily prices (features.incremental_prices). On: each run asks Yahoo only for the days since the last saved bar, starting overlap_days calendar days earlier, and merges those bars into cache/ohlcv.csv.gz. Older bars stay, so a short download cannot wipe a stock. The newest bar is not part of the adjustment check, because it is still forming during the day. An older overlap close that moved by more than the wider of adjust_tolerance_dollars and adjust_tolerance_pct percent of the old close (0.05 means 0.05 percent, not 5 percent) is treated as a split or dividend adjustment, and that one symbol is downloaded again for history_period. repair (on) does that full download once for a symbol with fewer than repair_below_bars saved bars, such as a history cut down to a single day, and does not repeat it if the full download is still short. refresh (on) redownloads adjusted history on the after-close run only. refresh_mode weekly does everyone when the last full refresh is at least refresh_every_days old. refresh_mode slice does one of refresh_slices slices each after-close run. The first full run after this is turned on starts the weekly clock and does not redownload five years that day. chart_concurrency is how many chart calls run at once (1 or 2). The same backoff as the rest of the desk still applies. backfill_per_run (40) is how many brand-new names a regular 10:15 or 18:30 run downloads in full. features.fast_history_backfill (on) is the one-time catch-up: stock_desk.py --backfill, and the Fill new price history workflow, download fast_backfill_per_run (600) names that have no saved bars, two chart calls at a time, and may chain up to fast_backfill_max_runs (4) runs. That path does not fetch profiles, filings, news, or options, and it does not raise the cap on the regular runs. Turn the switch off after the new names have history. Off: every run downloads history_period for every symbol with the old parallel download and replaces the price file.
